story.head: The Jets come in hot
paras: The Jets have won five straight, the last an 8-3 rout of Dallas, and they’re rolling. The Islanders (8-6-4) beat Los Angeles 5-2 on Nov 12. Going in, the Isles are fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 18th in the NHL) and the Jets sixth in the Central (tied for 16th).
The Islanders’ record (.556) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.473), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Jets’ record (.525) is about what their chances are worth.

The Islanders have had the league’s best goaltending (1st), spread the ice time through the lineup (2nd) and get their defensemen shooting (3rd). As for the Jets, they ice the puck less than anyone (1st), create chances on the penalty kill (3rd) and get their shots through to the net (3rd).

Bo Horvat (8 G / 10 A / 18 P in 18 GP) is tied for the Islanders’ scoring lead. Matthew Schaefer (6 G / 12 A / 18 P in 18 GP) shares it. For the Jets, Kyle Connor (16 G / 8 A / 24 P in 20 GP) leads the way in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Mark Scheifele (6 G / 16 A / 22 P in 20 GP) is next in line, with ten points in his last five games.

Ilya Sorokin (7-4-2 / .915 SV% in 13 GS) has been a rock in net for the Islanders and will likely start. Stuart Skinner (7-4-3 / .886 SV% in 14 GS) is in line to start for Winnipeg. Sorokin has a .876 save percentage in five starts against the Jets, well under his usual .909. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
At home, Scott Arniel likes to send Koepke, Barron and Rosén out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Palát, Cizikas and Duclair.

items.text: The Islanders have been without Mathew Barzal all season.
The Jets are newly without Dylan DeMelo, and have been without Elias Salomonsson and Clay Stevenson for several games. Stuart Skinner is expected to start.
Gabriel Vilardi has two goals on chances worth about 6.1 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Victor Eklund has scored in four straight games.
